summary: SomaHealth: semantic accuracy drop after enabling adaptive async batching + 4-bit quant + KV TTL eviction
description: Issue opened by SomaHealth CS: after enabling the new adaptive async batching policy (per-request grouping) together with the new 4-bit quantization profile and the kv-cache TTL eviction (LRU-timeout=30s) for tenant somahealth-prod, several endpoints show increased semantic errors and hallucinations for a critical clinical extraction prompt set. Customer observed sudden mismatch between human-labeled expected extraction values and model outputs starting 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC after a config rollout. They want guidance for immediate safe rollback and root-cause investigation.
impact: Customer reports ~15 percentage point drop in exact-match extraction accuracy on their 250-example evaluation set (from 91% -> 76%). Production traffic includes ~1200 requests/min for affected routes; some requests are latency-sensitive (95th p50-95 target 200-500ms). Business impact: triaged as P1 due to potential clinical safety risk and SLA exposure.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant somahealth-prod has optimizer profile 'adaptive-async-batch-v2' enabled, quant-profile 'q4-dense-agg', and kv-eviction 'lru-ttl=30s'.
2) Send the customer's canonical extraction prompt with patient note payload (attached in logs).
3) Compare token-level outputs and structured extraction fields to expected gold labels.
4) Re-run against the same model with quant-profile 'q8-normal' and batching disabled — outputs align with expected labels.
logs: Attached snippets from request IDs: req-20260312-11a, req-20260312-11b. Example mismatch: expected 'medication_dose: 5 mg' returned 'dose: 5mg twice' causing parser mismatch. Console traces show 'batch_group_id' assigned, 'kv_cache_hit=false' in many failing requests. No 5xxs reported. Latency profiles show slight increase in p95 (~+40ms) during incident window.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Quantization to 4-bit changed tokenization/post-decoding behavior for rare clinical tokens leading to extraction errors. 2) Adaptive async batching combined with short KV TTL may produce stale/misaligned KV contexts for requests that relied on prefix cache warmups. 3) Race conditions in batch packing could reorder prompt segments for this tenant due to payload chunking. Current telemetry: precision drop correlates with rollout time; failing requests largely show kv_cache_hit=false and grouping into larger async batches. We inspected PR #6124 which enabled new packing heuristics and found a non-deterministic padding path that may affect token alignment for long clinical notes.
comments: Customer (SomaHealth CS): 'We validated on a mirror and see divergence only when q4 + adaptive async batching is on.'
Support (Ava): 'Collecting failing request IDs and creating snapshot. We'll validate rollback steps; assigning to runtime team.'
Eng (Liam): 'I will reproduce on staging, capture kernel-level traces, and prepare a safe rollback plan. Suspect packing heuristics + quantization interplay.'
SRE (Mira): 'Recommend immediate traffic-splitting to fallback model variant and disable kv-eviction for somahealth-prod while investigation continues.'
workaround: Apply temporary traffic-split: 95% -> hf/soma-med-13b-v1 (q8-normal), 5% -> current variant for warm monitoring. Disable kv-eviction for tenant somahealth-prod (set lru-ttl=600s) to avoid repeated cold-cache misses. Disable adaptive-async-batch flag per-tenant until controlled verification.
rollback_steps: 1) Snapshot current config: redwoodctl config snapshot create --tenant somahealth-prod --name pre-rollback-20260312
2) Create traffic gate: redwoodctl traffic split set --tenant somahealth-prod --route /extract --split 'variant_q8:0.95,variant_q4:0.05'
3) Disable adaptive async batching: redwoodctl optimizer set --tenant somahealth-prod --profile adaptive-async-batch-v2 --enabled false
4) Revert quant profile: redwoodctl model pin --tenant somahealth-prod --model hf/soma-med-13b-v1 --quant q8-normal
5) Increase kv-cache ttl: redwoodctl cache set --tenant somahealth-prod --kv-ttl 600
6) Monitor 5m rolling accuracy on customer's evaluation set via console/dashboard and hold changes if regression persists
resolution: (TBD) Initial mitigation applied: traffic-split and increased kv-ttl. Early telemetry shows accuracy improved to 89% on customer's eval within 30 minutes after rollback steps 2-4. Ongoing root-cause: engineering to instrument kernel dequant path and packing order. Will plan full rollback if improvement not stable. Postmortem scheduled if confirmed causal link to packing heuristics and 4-bit quant interactions.
